subject.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw accept broad literal `agents.list[].env` for all supported child-process families, or should this PR be narrowed/deferred in favor of the exec-only SecretRef contract from #96309?
rationale: The code path is technically coherent, but the permanent public config and credential-boundary shape is a product/security decision that automation should not choose.

options.title: Choose the canonical env contract before merge
options.body: Require maintainer agreement on broad `agents.list[].env` versus the narrower exec-only SecretRef model, then align this PR to that chosen contract before landing.

options.title: Accept broad sanitized per-agent env
options.body: Land this PR as the canonical literal per-agent env surface and own the compatibility/security semantics for all wired child-process families.

options.title: Pause behind the exec-only design
options.body: Keep or close this PR after #96309 or a successor settles the narrower SecretRef-based exec environment direction.

recommendation.title: Choose the canonical env contract before merge
recommendation.body: Require maintainer agreement on broad `agents.list[].env` versus the narrower exec-only SecretRef model, then align this PR to that chosen contract before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to prior guidance on the earlier per-agent env attempt and has relevant recent config/agent history, making them the best available owner for the API-shape decision.
